name: S-Class Characters: The Monster Trainer
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced. The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—a summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

S-class s-class monster trainers are the most elite of their kind; traveling the shattered worlds in search of new and interesting monsters to bring back with them into the Kingdom. The bond they share with their captured monsters traverses even the planes of existence.

Note: With one exception, the s-class monster trainer is an alternate, superior version of the monster trainer class.

They retain all of the standard trainer progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select monster trainer archetypes without specific adjustments. If an archetype feature alters or replaces trainer perks, the s-class monster trainer gains that feature starting at 3rd level and every odd level thereafter.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8.

Starting Wealth: 4d6 × 10 gp (average 140 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class monster trainer’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), fly (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), and Survival (Wis).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class monster trainer.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

S-class monster trainers are proficient with all simple and martial weapons. They are proficient with light armor, and with shields (but not tower shields). A trainer can cast trainer spells while wearing light armor or using a shield without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, a trainer wearing medium or heavy armor, incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has any somatic components. A multiclass trainer still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes.

Spellcasting

An s-class monster trainer casts arcane spells that she gains from the monsters she captures. When a trainer controls a monster that grants her spells in some way, the trainer gains the ability to cast those spells as a sorcerer of her same level. She also gains the ability to cast that monster’s 0-level spells (cantrips) at will, if it provides any.

An s-class monster trainer can cast any spell she has access to without preparing it ahead of time. To gain access to or cast a spell, a trainer must have an active monster that grants the spell and a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a trainer’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the trainer’s Charisma modifier

Like other spellcasters, an s-class monster trainer can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table: S-Class Monster Trainer. In addition, she receives bonus spells per day if she has a high Charisma score.

Cantrips: An s-class monster trainer automatically knows and can cast any cantrips granted by her active monster.
Eschew Materials: S-class s-class monster trainers gain Eschew Materials as a bonus feat at 1st level, which allows them to ignore the common material components of the spells their monsters grant them.
Point of Origin: The trainer can cast her spells through her active monster, using its space as the point of origin to determine her line of sight and effect as the spell is cast (as if she were in the space in that moment). This doesn’t grant the trainer any of her active monster’s special senses, however. Because it is physically in the space when the spell is cast, the trainer’s monster draws any attacks of opportunity, not the trainer herself. The trainer can still cast defensively to avoid harming her monster, and must still make a concentration check if either is damaged while casting.
Capture Monster (Sp)

Every s-class monster trainer knows and can cast the capture monster spell at will and may heighten that spell as if she possessed the Heighten Spell metamagic feat. At 1st level, an s-class monster trainer has already either captured her first monster or been given one by a mentor such as a monster researcher.

Capturing Unconventional Creatures: An s-class monster trainer can accept willing creatures into her essence without casting capture monster. In this way, she can obtain creatures not usually considered monsters. A charmed or dominated creature does not have the capacity to willingly accept capture.

The trainer can also obtain monsters from other trainers as an exchange or gift. Accepting willing monsters into her essence has no direct cost (although some trainers are known to buy and sell captured monsters), and takes 1 minute per CR of the highest CR monster being gifted or exchanged.

Monster Training (Ex)

Monster training is the act of calling, controlling, and recalling monsters in or out of combat.

Calling Monsters: As a move action, an s-class monster trainer can call upon one of her monsters. This is identical to drawing a weapon, except that the trainer doesn’t need a +1 base attack to call upon her monster while moving.

An s-class monster trainer with Quick Draw can call upon a monster as a free action.

Calling upon even one monster is a rigorous mental activity, and if the trainer is unable to take 10 on actions, she cannot call upon more than one monster at a time. When faced with an immediate threat or distraction, all but one monster of the trainer’s choice are returned to her essence as a free action.

When first called upon, the now active monster appears in an unoccupied space within 10 ft. of its trainer with hit points equal to the trainer’s current hit points (anything over the monster’s total hit points are considered temporary, and anything under can be healed as normal). If no such space exists where the monster can fit, the ability fails and the action is lost.

Controlling Monsters: In the same way a human fighter can’t wield a bow and a greatsword at the same time, a trainer can only give her attention to one monster at a time in combat.

Unlike a wizard’s familiar or a druid’s animal companion, a trainer’s monster does not gain its own actions during combat. Once the monster appears, the trainer uses her own actions to direct and communicate with it telepathically out to 100 feet. The monster doesn’t gain actions or special (Sp, Su, or Ex) abilities of its own, only those granted by the trainer. If the trainer is reduced to 0 or fewer hit points but not dead, she can still direct her active monster to take a single move or standard action on each of her turns.

Recalling Monsters: The trainer can use her telepathic bond to call her active monster back into her essence as a move action, equivalent to sheathing a weapon. When a monster is recalled, it fades away from reality, disappearing entirely. The trainer’s hit points are reduced to match the monster’s remaining hp if lower than her own (this loss of hit points cannot be redirected or reduced), and all negative effects on the monster are removed, as with a heal spell. If a monster is reduced to 0 or fewer hit points, it is immediately recalled from any distance at 0 hit points as a free action. If a trainer dies, her monster fades back into her essence as a free action. A trainer’s spirit can still gift monsters to other trainers if they have a means of communicating with it.

Downtime Activities: During downtime, a trainer can call upon some or all of her monsters to spend time with them; training animals, playing, interacting with or showing her monsters off to others. Doing so requires the trainer’s full attention and gives no special benefit to the monster trainer, so she can’t also work or progress in crafting items.

A trainer’s monsters with 2 or lower Intelligence (or Int –) gain the attack trick twice automatically when captured, but must still be trained to perform other tasks. The trainer can use the training process and Handle Animal to teach tricks to any of her captured monsters with Intelligence 2 or less (mindless creatures count as having an Intelligence of 1 for this purpose).

Trainer Aura (Ex)

The alignment displayed by the monster trainer’s aura can be misleading because it is affected by the monsters she has captured. A creature observing the trainer’s aura will see a muddled mix of alignments, though often one will stand out more prominently, such as when a trainer captures a majority of evil monsters. Anybody attempting to detect a trainer’s alignment requires a number of additional rounds equal to one-half the trainer’s level (minimum 1) to do so.

The trainer determines the exact visual nature of her aura. For example, the trainer’s aura can appear to be a swirl of energy around her head or a pouch of orbs at her waist containing each monster she’s captured. The trainer can make her aura visible, though it provides no mechanical benefit to do so.

Favored Enemy (Ex)

At 2nd level, an s-class monster trainer selects a creature type from the ranger’s favored enemies list. If she chooses outsiders as a favored enemy, she must also choose an associated subtype. If a specific creature falls into more than one category of favored enemy, the favored enemy bonuses do not stack.

The trainer gains a +2 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks against all of her favored enemies. Likewise, she gets a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against them. An s-class monster trainer may make Knowledge skill checks untrained when attempting to identify these creatures.

At 5th, 10th, and 15th level, the trainer may select an additional favored enemy. In addition, at each such interval, the bonus against all of her favored enemies increases by +1.

Restrictions: S-class s-class monster trainers can’t apply their favored enemy bonuses against any creature that isn’t considered a monster. For this reason, they almost never choose humanoids, and only rarely choose monstrous humanoids. Monstrous humanoids in Eldura that don’t become monstorin are closer to magical beasts. On other worlds, most monstrous humanoids would be considered monstorin already by trainers because of their complex auras.

Monster Growth (Ex)

Starting at 2nd level, when she gains a new trainer level, an s-class monster trainer can improve one of the monsters she has obtained (through capture or otherwise). If the trainer doesn’t have a monster that can grow at a given level, she can hold onto this ability until she captures a compatible monster or reaches a high enough level to help one or more other monsters to grow. Monster growth allows a trainer to choose a monster with a similar heritage to a monster she captured previously and begin using that monster instead. This change is generally permanent, so trainer’s are always encouraged to think carefully before making such a decision.

Spell Familiarity

At 2nd level, and every even level thereafter, an s-class monster trainer chooses one spell granted to her by a monster she has captured. She can now cast that spell regardless of the monster she has active. At the time she gains these new spells, the monster trainer can also swap one previous spell gained with spell familiarity for another of the same level.

Empathy (Ex)

An s-class monster trainer can improve the attitude of any monster type she counts as a favored enemy. This ability functions just like a Diplomacy check made to improve the attitude of a person. The trainer rolls 1d20 and adds her monster trainer level and her Charisma modifier to determine the empathy check result.

The typical monster has a starting attitude of indifferent, while more feral monsters are usually unfriendly at best.

To use empathy, the trainer and the monster must be able to study each other, which means that they must be within 30 feet of one another under normal conditions. Generally, influencing a monster in this way takes 1 minute but, as with influencing people, it might take more or less time.

Talented Trainer

Starting at 3rd level, the trainer can direct her active monster to use its special attacks, defenses, and abilities a number of times per day equal to her Charisma modifier + 1/2 her monster trainer level. Those abilities must have an immediate effect on combat (afflictions, curses, diseases, and poisons are not typically gained with talented trainer).

If the monster has any special abilities that act like spells, it can’t use those abilities until the trainer could cast spells of that level. Spells not found on the trainer’s spell list are treated as one level higher than the highest level at which a class could cast them.

The trainer can direct her monster to use its spell-like abilities at 3rd level, supernatural abilities at 7th level, and extraordinary abilities at 11th level. The trainer can also use these abilities herself, acting as their point of origin.

In addition to her daily limitation, the trainer and her monster share any other restrictions on abilities. For example, if the trainer uses her dragon’s breath weapon, she and the monster must both wait 1d4 rounds before one of them can use it again. Constant effects (but not senses) are shared, but abilities listed in a monster’s stat block as (self only) can only be used by the monster and only while it is active.

Trainer Perks

At 3rd level, and every odd level thereafter, an s-class monster trainer gains a perk that she can use whenever she has any monster active. A sample listing of trainer perks can be found at the end of this section.

Shared Senses (Su)

Starting at 5th level, the monster trainer and her active monster share their senses, including blindsight, darkvision, low-light vision, scent, tremorsense, and true seeing. This doesn’t allow them to see through each other’s eyes, but they can still communicate their observations telepathically.

Trainer’s Edge (Ex)

At 6th level, an s-class monster trainer chooses a skill possessed by one or more of her monsters. When she calls upon a monster with that skill, the trainer gains the skill unlock powers for the chosen skill as appropriate for the number of ranks in that skill she or her monster has, whichever is higher. At 11th level, she chooses an additional skill and gains skill unlock powers for that skill as well when her active monster has it.

Great Trainer (Ex)

At 9th level, an s-class monster trainer can spend 1 use of talented trainer to cast a heightened capture monster spell as a standard action (or as a swift action if she also applies Quicken Spell).

Temporary Control (Sp)

Beginning at 10th level, the monster trainer can spend 1 use of talented trainer to cast charm monster as a spell-like ability. The spell only works on monsters she can capture and lasts only up to 1 round per level. The trainer cannot have another monster active when using temporary control.

Channel Monster (Ex)

At 13th-level, an s-class monster trainer has learned how to shape her essence without a monster to draw from. Each morning, when she regains spells, the trainer chooses one monster she has captured. When she has no other active monster, the trainer can cast spells from the chosen monster’s trainer spell list as if it were her active monster.

Swap Monster (Ex)

Once per day at 15th level, When the monster trainer calls her active monster back into her essence, she can call upon a new monster as part of the same action. If she does, the trainer can apply her previous monster’s remaining hp (if lower than her current hit points) to the new monster, rather than herself.

Perfect Capture (Ex)

When the monster trainer reaches 17th level, she learns a special secret that has eluded most trainers their entire lives.

She can now capture a single monster without any saves or checks. She can do this once, and the monster must still be one she is able to capture. If the trainer ever releases the monster captured in this way, she regains master trainer the next time she rests for at least 8 hours.

If able, a monster released from master trainer returns to the location from which it was captured, traversing planes to do so if it must. If it is unable to return, the monster instead appears in a space adjacent to the trainer, free to do as it wishes.

Cunning monsters previously captured with master trainer may sometimes seek the trainer out once more in order to punish her for capturing them in the first place.

Master Trainer

At 20th level, an s-class monster trainer has achieved her lifelong dream of becoming a master trainer, recognized for her skill and talents across the region. She gains her choice of one master perk or three trainer perks.

Trainer Perks
Standard Trainer Perks
Downtime Ally (Ex)

You can direct up to 2 of your active monsters during downtime to assist you with tasks such as training other monsters, crafting, or working. Your monsters are still recalled if you become distracted or threatened with combat.

Evasion (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 2nd level.

You gain evasion, as the monk class feature. You can avoid damage from many area-effect attacks. If you make a successful Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, you instead takes no damage. Evasion can be used only if you are wearing light armor or no armor. You don’t gain the benefit of evasion when you are helpless.

Evasion, Improved (Ex)

Requires 8th level and Evasion. You gain improved evasion, as the monk class feature. When you fail a Reflex saving throw with evasion, you only take half damage.

Extended Calling (Su)

When you call upon a monster, you can choose for it to appear anywhere within 30 ft. of you.

Fuse Monsters (Su)

As a full-round action, you can call upon and fuse two monsters into one for up to 1 round per trainer level. The CR of each monster must be within 3 of the other. Choose one monster as the base for the fusion, and the following from the second monster. At the end of the duration, the secondary monster returns to your essence.

Choose defenses or offensive abilities

Defenses include AC, CMD, DR, hp, immunities, resistances, saves, SR, and weaknesses. If the monster has any specifically defensive feats, they are included in this option.
Offensive abilities include melee and ranged attacks, initiative, CMB, and abilities directly related to attacks, such as bleed, rend, or trample.

Choose special abilities or trainer spells

Special abilities include anything the monster can do offensively or defensively beyond the above, such as an aura, a breath weapon, or other extraordinary and supernatural abilities. The trainer spells feature and spell-like abilities are not included here.
Trainer spells include any spell-like abilities the monster gains, as well as the trainer spell list it grants.

The fusion also gains all senses and skills from both monsters. If either monster’s trainer spells are restricted (0 through 6th or 1st through 4th), the fusion’s spells are likewise limited, even if you don’t choose the trainer spells option. You cannot fuse already fused monsters.

The fused monster gains the chosen options in place of its own, even if they are worse than it would normally have.

For easy reference, several fused monsters can be found in the next section. Those monsters can be captured on their own, in which case their essences are permanently fused and they can only be called upon that way.

Fusion Expert (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Fuse Monsters trainer perk.

When you have an active fused monster, you can change the secondary monster for another in the same way you would call upon a different monster in combat. The choices you made when calling upon the fused monster remain, but are applied to the new secondary monster instead. This feature does not function on permanently fused monsters.

Permanent Fusion (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Fuse Monsters trainer perk.

Choose two monsters you have previously fused when calling upon them. You can permanently entwine those monsters, creating a stable fusion that you can call upon normally as its own monster. The new monster’s effective CR is equal to half the combined CR of the base monsters, rounded up. The base monsters are no longer available for you to call upon, but their essence still exists together, allowing you to still share their memories before and after they were fused. You can select this perk more than once.

Run With Me (Ex)

When you move as a move action, your active monster can also move up to half its speed as part of the same action and vice versa. You can select this perk twice, at which point you and your active monster can move at full speed instead.

Skilled Trainer (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): You must have captured at least 3 monsters.

Combining your essence with so many different monsters makes you especially good at adapting to new skills. You gain skill ranks equal to twice your monster trainer level.

When you gain a new level of monster trainer, you gain 2 additional skill ranks.

Swift Attack (Ex)

When you direct your active monster to take a full attack action, you can also make a single attack as a swift action.

When you take a full attack action, you can also direct your active monster to make a single attack as a swift action. All attacks made by you and your monster this round are made at a –2 penalty.

Tough Companion (Ex)

When you call upon a monster, it appears with hit points equal to your current hit points + your monster trainer level, if it would begin with fewer hit points.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

You and your active monster each gain Uncanny Dodge, as the rogue ability of the same name. You cannot be caught flat-footed, nor do you lose your Dex bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. You still lose your Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. You can still lose your Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against you.

Uncanny Dodge, Improved (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Uncanny Dodge

You and your active monster each gain improved uncanny dodge, as the rogue ability of the same name. You deny rogues the ability to sneak attack you or your monster when flanking, unless the attacker has at least four more rogue levels than your monster trainer level.

Master Trainer Perks
Superior Fusion

Prerequisite(s): Fuse Monsters trainer perk.

When you call upon a fused monster, the base monster retains its special abilities and trainer spells, in addition to gaining the option chosen for the secondary monster. Spell limitations still take effect, and abilities that directly oppose each other can’t be used within 1d4 round of each other.

If you have any permanently fused monsters, they gain back any special abilites or trainer spells they gave up when originally fused.

Fused Monsters
Companion Monster – Lucatile

Lucatile was a pair of monsters that found their way into the Kingdom one of the many times their fellow monster, celedeen traveled there over the years. In their struggle to survive in the dangerous, new world, the monsters permanently fused into one.

After the Collective established a stable connection with Eldura, some of the monsters that remembered the original pair came to find them. When they returned home with news of their fellow monsters’ fate, some of their kind chose to honor their lost brethren by fusing as well, creating the first full family of permanently fused monsters that would become known to monster trainers as lucatiles.

Lucatile Monstorin Heritage Traits (10 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: +2 Dexterity, +2 Wisdom (2 RP): Lucatile monstorin have good reactions and are spiritually balanced.
Size: Medium (0 RP). Lucatiles have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Speed: Fast Movement (1 RP). Lucatiles have a base speed of 40 feet.
Senses: Low-light vision (1 RP). A lucatile can see twice as far as a human in conditions of dim light.
Languages (0 RP): Common. Lucatiles with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Elven, Giant, Sylvan.
Monstorin (0 RP): Lucatiles are humanoids with the monstorin subtyp.
Aura Reader (3 RP, Su): As a standard action, a lucatile can detect creatures of one alignment type it chooses within 30 feet. This lasts for up to 1 minute per character level, and must be spent in 1-minute increments. It otherwise functions as the appropriate detect spell.
Immunities (2 RP): Lucatiles are immune to magic sleep effects. They also gain a +2 racial saving throw bonus against enchantment spells and effects.
Plant Resistances (1 RP): Because they are part plant, lucatiles have resist electricity 5.
Fire Vulnerability (–2 RP): All lucatiles have vulnerability to fire damage.
Monstorin Favored Class Bonuses
Brawler: Deal +1 damage against undead with ki blast and +1/3 damage against other creatures.
Monk: Deal +1 damage against undead with ki blast and +1/3 damage against other creatures.

New Ancestry Feat Ki Blast

Prerequisite(s): Wis 13, monstorin ancestry, lucatile monstorin heritage.

Benefit(s): You can create a ki blast once every 1d4 rounds. This is a ranged weapon with a 50-ft. range increment that deals 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier bludgeoning damage on a hit. The damage increases by 2d6 at 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 10d6 at 18th level.

Special: When your base attack bonus is +11 or higher, you can use ki blast a second time in the same round as part of a fullattack action, but the second attack is made with a –5 penalty. You must still wait 1d4 rounds before using it again.

Fel’cu

The fusion of a fel’kraz with an elcu is a dangerous, ghostly monster able to possess objects and wait in hiding until it detects a child nearby that it can feed off of. The Kingdom’s researchers have issued strong warnings against releasing this fused monster anywhere near society, if at all.

Fel’cu CR 5 (XP 1,600)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Ghostly Games (Sp)

As a full round action, a fel’cu can take possession of an unattended large or smaller object.

This turns the elcu into an animated object of the appropriate size for up to one round per hit dice of the elcu. Once the duration is up, the object is destroyed, or the elcu otherwise leaves the object, it can escape on its next turn, taking half the damage dealt to the object it possessed in the process.

Spine Tingler (Su)

A living creature touched by a fel’cu must make a DC 15 Fortitude save or immediately drops anything it is holding and fall prone, shivering for 1 round. It is not helpless but is unable to make any actions during this round. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Displaced (Su)

When hit by a magic, corporeal attack or spell, a cuytharion has a 50% chance to take half damage.

When attacking an incorporeal creature, it only has a 50% chance to deal half damage. Antimagic fields make a cuytharion incorporeal.

Marionette Armor (Su)

A creature that puts on a cuytharion’s armor while the monster is dormant must make a Will save (DC 18) or be subject to a marionette possession spell for up to 90 minutes. Every 30 minutes, the creature can attempt its save again to break the effect and take off the armor.
